category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting inappropriate physical contact and out-of-seat behavior
minimal_context: Matthew is joining a group of children in a mainstream classroom setting for a social reading activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Matthew, it is time to join the group for our reading activity.

STUDENT: (Walks toward the group, staring closely at a classmate who is wearing sparkly hair grips.)

TUTOR: Find an empty seat next to the others.

STUDENT: (Continues approaching the classmate, causing the other children to move away and avoid interacting with him.)

TUTOR: Matthew, please just sit down.

STUDENT: (Reaches out to touch and flick the classmate's hair without permission, causing her to scream as he approaches.)

options.A: Rotate the staff-to-pupil assignment on a daily or weekly basis during the mainstream classroom sessions and social reading activities.
options.B: Use applications like Look2Learn and Stories2Learn to create personalized stories with recorded photos and audio for the daily social reading activity.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each social reading task during the daily school sessions in the mainstream classroom.
options.D: Extend the behavior contract to include inappropriate touching of hair once out-of-seat behavior decreases to zero, concurrently increasing the reward to fifteen minutes of home computer access.
